name: AudioFix — Podcast Loudness Fix & Re-Check (Local, Private)
description:
Why does my podcast sound too quiet on Spotify and too loud on Apple — and how do I fix its loudness to match each platform?
AudioFix measures your episode with the same loudnorm analysis the platforms use, normalizes it to the target, then RE-MEASURES the finished file and shows you the before/after numbers with a plain PASS / NOT READY verdict.
PRESETS
• Podcast — −16 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1 dB
• Streaming / YouTube — −14 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1 dB
• Audiobook (ACX-style) — −20 LUFS, true peak ≤ −3 dB
WHAT IT DOES
• Two-pass loudnorm normalization based on your file's actual measurements
• Optional trim of leading/trailing silence
• Re-check on the output: loudness within ±0.5 LUFS and peak under the ceiling, or it tells you exactly which failed
• Flags recorded clipping honestly — no tool can un-clip audio, and this one won't pretend
VERIFIED, NOT VIBES
Seeded test recording at −29.9 LUFS with 4 s of edge silence: trimmed to length and normalized to −15.9 LUFS against the −16 target, verified by re-measuring the output. Verdict: PASS.
100% LOCAL & PRIVATE — no upload, no per-hour credits, no subscription. Your unreleased episodes never leave your computer. (Upload-based loudness services charge by the hour of audio; this is one payment, forever.)
Windows 10/11, ffmpeg bundled — nothing else to install. Works on mp3 / wav / m4a / mp4 and anything else ffmpeg reads.
Scope: overall loudness, true peak, edge silence. It doesn't remove background noise or echo — those are recording problems.
